claims.text: Every Pod gets a unique cluster-wide IP; all Pods reach all Pods, same or different node, directly, without proxies or NAT, so a server sees the caller's Pod IP as source (unlike networks that replace it with the leaving machine's address).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Services, Load Balancing, and Networking (The Kubernetes network model)

claims.text: Kubernetes defines the network model rules but does not wire Pods together itself: a pod network implementation, chosen when the cluster is built, makes them true on each node.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: The Kubernetes network model ('pod network ... implemented by'); Cluster Networking; Network Plugins

claims.text: A Pod's IP address is in status.podIP; Pods are ephemeral, a replacement Pod is a new Pod, and you cannot count on it getting the same address.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Pod API reference (PodStatus.podIP); Concepts > Services (Pods are ephemeral, IPs change)

claims.text: Node spec.podCIDR is the Pod IP range assigned to the node. Attributed to the reader's own run (masked in the capture): each Pod's address falls inside the podCIDR of the node that runs it, so a Pod's address tells its node.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Node API reference (NodeSpec.podCIDR); kind.sigs.k8s.io (kindnet, host-local IPAM per node podCIDR)

claims.text: CIDR notation: 10.244.2.0/24 covers the addresses 10.244.2.0 to 10.244.2.255.
Containers within a Pod share a network namespace, including the IP address and network ports, and communicate with one another using localhost; two of them cannot listen on the same port.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Workloads > Pods ('Pod networking'); Cluster Networking (container-to-container via localhost)

claims.text: Without NetworkPolicies, every Pod accepts connections from every other Pod in the cluster; NetworkPolicies limit this.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Network Policies ('The two sorts of pod isolation', non-isolated by default)
